title: MESH render patches, version 1
description: What the MESH runtime's update produces (see docs/manual/runtime.md, "Update"): the operations that turn the previous render's tree into the new render's tree, when both come from one program. A renderer applies them in order. The law: applying them to the previous tree gives exactly the tree a full render of the new snapshot gives. A list is minimal in effect, not unique in form, so a renderer applies lists and never compares them. Nodes and text runs are named by their render-v1 keys, which the renderer compares only for equality; a key is the identity of MESH spec §9.10, and parts are matched by key and never by position. A prop or text a patch doesn't mention is unchanged. Removals come first, then the insertions and moves that put the kept parts in the new order (each `before` names a sibling that exists at that point in the list, or is absent for last), then the changes inside the kept parts. A key that is removed and later appears again is a new part, not the old one. `replace` is for a tree no other operation can turn into the next (a different root, or a node whose event bindings differ, which one program never produces): draw it afresh, reusing nothing, and it is always the only operation of its list. This schema lists exactly the properties this MESH produces. A later MESH may add operations or properties without changing `version`, but a renderer that meets an operation it doesn't know must refuse the list, never skip it, since skipping would break the law; removing a property or changing a meaning is a new version. A later MESH may add properties without changing `version`, so consumers should ignore properties they don't know.

key.description: A render-v1 key: a node's or text run's identity. Compare for equality only.

oneOf.description: The prop now has this value, and this MESH text if it has one (`propText`, as render-v1 carries it); a prop with no `propText` has none now.
The prop is now absent, with its text.

A node or text run, with everything under it, is new under the node `parent`: before its child `before`, or last when `before` is absent. The `node` is a render-v1 node (with its whole subtree) or text run, whose keys are not in the tree at this point.
The node or text run, and everything under it, is gone.
The same node or text run, kept with everything under it, now stands before its sibling `before`, or last when `before` is absent.
The tree is this one: draw it afresh, as for a program change, reusing nothing.
